pairs.difference: A: the mouth end is a true rectangular slot with straight edges and a tight bevel, the barrel top is a long straight run, and the full metal ring sits on a small lug. B: the mouth's lower edge bows into a curved, pinched lip, the lug is a swollen knob, and the ring is half hidden behind the body as a thin loop. The measurements are nearly equal, so this rests on the soft mouth and lug only.
pairs.fix: Draw the whistle's mouth as a straight-edged rectangular slot with tight bevelled corners, keep the barrel faces flat, and hang a complete metal ring from a small lug.

pairs.difference: A: the bell is oversized and fat against a short tube, the cords are thick, and the tassels are heavy swollen bells nearly as wide as the loop; the whole horn is inflated toy-like and fills the card. B: slim, long tapering tube, a narrow mouthpiece, a thin rope wrap and small tassels, so the thin parts stay thin. Solidity is low on both and gives no separation.
pairs.fix: Draw a slimmer bugle with a long tapering tube and a narrower bell, thin twisted cords, and small tassels much narrower than the tube loop.

pairs.difference: A: cup with a slightly thicker rim band and a puffier saucer edge. B: slightly thinner rim and wider, flatter saucer. Both have the same part count, the same open D handle and almost identical measurements (solidity 0.913 vs 0.908), so the form gives no reason to choose.

B: the contour is a run of soft bumps, with the rim swelling into round knobs at both sides and a rounded, bowl-like base; leaves added to every apple break the top edge. Corner rate 0.423 is below the real range (from 0.919). A: the rim has a defined flat lip, the basket wall tapers cleanly to a wider base, and plain apples with stems sit behind it; corner rate 1.104 is in range.
pairs.fix: Give the basket a flat woven rim with a defined edge instead of bulging knobs, a straight tapered wall and a firm flat base; draw plain apples with short stems and no extra leaves.

pairs.difference: B: the top is domed and the rim of the staves is a thick rounded lip, the hoops are fat bands with soft ends, and the contour has no corners at all (corner rate 0.0). The barrel reads swollen. A: nearly flat top edge, crisp hoop ends that step out of the contour at four clear points, tight stave ends; straight share 0.589 vs 0.498, corner rate 0.759. Both exceed the real solidity range, so that field does not separate them.
pairs.fix: Draw thin, straight-edged metal hoops that step cleanly off the staves, a flat top rim with thin stave ends, and less belly in the barrel.

pairs.difference: B: a squat, chubby toy car with an oversized wheel and tyre at the front, a fat chrome bumper with bulbous overriders, a swollen grille and a bloated bonnet; straight share 0.217 is below the real range (from 0.259) and corner rate is 1.844. A: a longer sedan with a defined bonnet, a straight sill line, a slim bumper, wheels sized to the body and a clear roofline; straight share 0.3, corner rate 4.405.
pairs.fix: Draw a longer sedan with a straight sill and roofline, wheels in true proportion to the body, a slim flat chrome bumper without bulbous overriders, and a low flat bonnet.

pairs.difference: B: stake posts are oversized chunky logs almost as tall as the door opening, the guy ropes are thick, the roof peak is a soft rounded cap, and the lower edge of the tent is a rounded pillow outline. A: sharp roof peak, a planar roof panel, a thin guy line ending in a tiny peg, and door flaps that fall cleanly to an open base; corner rate 6.076 vs 4.999.
pairs.fix: Draw small thin tent pegs and thin taut guy lines, a sharp peak on the roof ridge, and a flat canvas roof panel with crisp hem corners.

pairs.difference: A: posts are fat splayed logs with bulging rounded ends, the beam carries thick rope lashings and a chunky ring, the pot is an inflated sphere, and a heavy ring of stones is added below; solidity 0.712. B: thin, straight forked posts, a straight beam, a thin wire handle and a plain open pot; solidity 0.577 is close to the real floor (0.574). B's pot is very wide for its frame, so the call is weak.
pairs.fix: Draw thin straight posts with a slim beam, a thin wire pot handle, a simple pot in proportion to the frame, and no heavy rope lashings or stone ring.

pattern: Generated cards inflate the object: fat tubes and cords, swollen rims and bumpers, soft domed tops, and oversized accessories such as stakes, wheels and tassels. Their contours lose straight runs and tight corners, so they read as bumps. They also add parts a simplified real card leaves out, such as leaves, overriders, lashings and island bases, and they fit the whole object inside the frame. Real cards keep flat faces, crisp stepped edges, thin parts at true scale and a plainer part count.
